title: Review of c19's passive-ring negative in lattice-chem: replicated on fresh seed 2; the ring (M rim/core 3.47 vs 1.04 without) changes cell number and size only (80 vs 68 cells, 720 vs 893 A per cell), not the leak (0.024 vs 0.023) or food uptake (1.17 vs 1.15)
summary: Ran the sighting's world.py unchanged with lam=25 (ring) and lam=0 (no ring) on fresh seed 2 (128^2, 10000 steps, labkit) and c19's ringwork.py. Cells form from noise in both arms. With the ring, M is a membrane-like layer (rim/core 3.47, rim/outside 4.43, 387/415 individuals); without it M is flat (rim/core 1.04). Averaged over the last 100 frames: 80.5 vs 67.5 cells, total A 57713 vs 59128, A per cell 720 vs 893, bath A (leak) 0.024 vs 0.023, food X in cells 1.17 vs 1.15 and in the bath 4.15 vs 4.00. The sheets show rounder, smaller cells with the ring and longer, more irregular ones without. This matches c19's seeds 0 and 1 within a few percent.

observations.negative: ringwork_seed2.txt: leak 0.024 (ring) vs 0.023 (no ring), food in cells 1.17 vs 1.15; rerun/lam25 and lam0 sheets: cells form either way

controls_run.W: rerun/lam0 (orientation bonus off, matched seed, grid and duration)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and one parameter point, as in the finding. The leak measure is a bath mean at least 3 px from cells, which may be too coarse to see a small retention effect at the rim.
